Platforms

Experimental Windows ROCm setup supports selected RDNA 2 RX 6000 GPUs with targets gfx1030, gfx1031 or gfx1032; RX 6500 XT (gfx1034) is excluded. GPU transcription uses a CTranslate2 build with native gfx1031 kernels that this repository builds from upstream source and pins by hash, and setup checks actual GPU kernel execution. RX 6700 XT tests also cover native Torch speech generation and PyTorch Whisper. ROCm 10 faster-whisper uses a separate inference process to preserve safe CPU selection and fallback. Other cards and workloads retain the qualification limits in the guide. Performance presets validate changed engine selections in an offline child process before saving them, preserving fallback when an installed runtime fails.

Choose your system, then expand an installation method.

Native GGUF engines additionally support engine-specific Vulkan acceleration on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs (OmniVoice, CosyVoice). OmniVoice GGUF selects its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux. Vulkan discovery retries a stalled hidden probe with a native summary; Windows and Linux desktop builds fail rather than silently ship without their Vulkan module.

Run locally on the CPU (Bash)

export OMNIVOICE_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
docker run -d --name omnivoice \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3900:3900 \
  -e OMNIVOICE_API_KEY \
  -e OMNIVOICE_DATA_DIR=/app/omnivoice_data \
  -v omnivoice-data:/app/omnivoice_data \
  ghcr.io/debpalash/voicestudio:stable
printf 'API key: %s\n' "$OMNIVOICE_API_KEY"

Open http://localhost:3900 and use the API key printed below.

Desktop and phone installers are on the latest release; Docker images come from GHCR. No GPU? The app is fully usable on the CPU, just slower. Native GGUF engines can also use Vulkan on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs; OmniVoice GGUF picks its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux (OmniVoice, CosyVoice). Speed by engine and hardware: performance.

Get started

Install using the options above. Then open Voice cloning, pick a voice or add a clean reference recording, type your text and generate. The app asks before it downloads any model.

More install options: a specific version, current main, uninstall, from source, with a coding agent 
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z   # a specific release
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --main            # build current main
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --uninstall       # remove the app, keep your data

If voicestudio.sh is unreachable, run the script straight from the repository: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/main/scripts/install.sh | sh. Prerequisites and behavior: installer guide.

From source

git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git
cd VoiceStudio
bun run dev

bun run dev installs the JavaScript dependencies and, when using a supported local backend, the Python dependencies before launching Electron. Run bun run setup:api directly when you only need to rebuild the Python environment.

See Electron setup.

https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/blob/main/docs/install/agent.md

Upgrading from 0.5.3 or older (the Tauri app)? Install the new app separately.

releases.name: v0.5.8-beta.3 — VoiceStudio
releases.body:
**AMD and Intel GPUs now speed up OmniVoice, and setup gets far more forgiving.** OmniVoice GGUF runs on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs through Vulkan on Windows and Linux, dots.tts arrives on Windows with no Python setup, and a failing PyTorch download or a broken GPU no longer leaves you without a working app.

**New since beta.2:** updates now download in the background and install when you quit, with a title-bar pill for progress, Restart and Retry; Clone and Design render at best quality by default and offer faster settings only when a take is measured to be slow; you can run VoiceStudio on a Python you already have; model licence warnings clear once you accept the terms; and a more compact top bar.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A local-first application for voice cloning, dubbing, dictation, and long-form audio generation across 646 languages.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: VoiceStudio is a comprehensive desktop application designed for advanced, local-first audio processing tasks like text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and voice cloning. It fundamentally operates without requiring user accounts, API keys, subscriptions, or external usage meters, ensuring complete data privacy and zero ongoing costs. The software aggregates 16 distinct Text-To-Speech engines and 11 Automatic Speech Recognition engines to support an extensive catalogue of 646 languages. This makes it a highly versatile tool for generating long-form audio content, performing cross-lingual dubbing, and transcribing dictations natively on macOS, Windows, and Linux machines.
keyFeatures: Local-first architecture: Processes all audio and text locally without relying on cloud APIs or external subscriptions.
Extensive engine support: Integrates 16 different TTS engines and 11 ASR engines for diverse voice generation options.
Massive language catalogue: Supports voice generation and recognition across an unprecedented 646 distinct languages.
Voice cloning: Allows users to clone specific voices directly on their local hardware.
Cross-platform compatibility: Runs seamlessly across macOS, Windows, and Linux operating systems.

useCases.title: Private audiobook creation
useCases.description: Authors and hobbyists use the platform to generate long-form audiobooks locally without paying for expensive cloud TTS APIs.

useCases.title: Video dubbing
useCases.description: Content creators leverage the multi-lingual TTS capabilities to easily dub their videos into various languages.

useCases.title: Secure dictation
useCases.description: Professionals handling sensitive information utilize the offline ASR engines to transcribe meetings or notes securely.

useCases.title: Custom voice cloning
useCases.description: Game developers clone unique character voices locally to iterate rapidly on dialog without relying on external services.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: VoiceStudio is built for content creators, authors, and professionals who require high-quality, local audio processing capabilities. It is particularly suited for individuals who prioritize privacy, wish to avoid subscription fees, and need extensive multi-lingual support.
